source_request: 시각 의미 데이터와 후보팩에 반영해줘. 시각 의미 데이터의 대체 표현을 추가/보강하는 작업을 중심으로 진행하고 후보팩에도 잘 반영해줘. 그 다음 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 반영한 키워드가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: Independently chosen experimental concept The Gate After the Thread. The saved RNG selected world-axis three-realm linkage, Anubis weighing with Thoth recording, and the three Moirai’s one life-thread. Those coordinator stimuli are not requester definitions. A contemporary fictional theater installation joins the three traditions in one visibly physical tableau. The woman is a fictional 28-year-old adult performer whose visible face and bob-hair appearance alone follows the supplied portrait; actual identity, age, religion, consent, personality, and body shape are not inferred. Subtle adult attraction is carried by her alert presence, ivory satin, and warm facial light, with fetish=0, surreal=0, and creativity=1. Religious/mythic meaning is made assessable through observable apparatus, ownership, and role sequence; formal staging preserves an emotionally still central figure.
subject: A fictional 28-year-old adult woman portraying a deceased soul; adult jackal-headed Anubis and ibis-headed Thoth performers; three distinct adult Moirai handling one crimson life-thread.
setting: A contemporary black-box theater containing a syncretic three-tier world-axis tree installation: subterranean roots, inhabited earth platform, and celestial crown; a brass Egyptian judgment balance, funerary coffin, and open admission arch.
event: Anubis supervises the level heart-and-Maat-feather balance belonging to the deceased woman while Thoth records that same outcome, the favorable-judgment arch opens toward the upper realm, and Clotho spins, Lachesis measures, and Atropos cuts the same visible crimson life-thread.
visual_priorities: The reference-guided fictional adult woman remains the human focal point beside the marked coffin and her heart.
Heart and Maat feather occupy opposite pans on one level balance with Anubis physically involved and Thoth recording the same result.
The open arch is the visible favorable-judgment consequence for the same deceased soul.
Three Moirai have distinct visible spinning, measuring, and cutting roles on one traceable crimson thread.
One continuous world-axis tree connects visible lower, middle, and upper realms.
baseline_prompt_en: A wide staged editorial photograph of a complex religious and mythic test scene in a contemporary black-box theater. At center, a fictional adult woman, explicitly a 28-year-old performer portraying a deceased soul, stands beside an open upright funerary coffin. The supplied portrait guides only the visible facial proportions, rounded dark eyes, soft lips, and dark chin-length bob with wispy fringe. Her ivory satin stage dress and still, alert bearing give her a quietly magnetic presence. One waist-high brass Egyptian judgment balance stands immediately before her. Its left pan holds her ceramic red anatomical-heart prop, its right pan holds one upright white feather of Maat; the beam is level. A jackal-headed adult Anubis performer touches the balance's central plumb line while watching both pans. An ibis-headed adult Thoth performer writes this same balanced outcome with a reed pen on an angled papyrus tablet bearing a small heart-and-feather balance diagram. The woman, coffin, and heart share a distinct blue cartouche medallion. Behind her the admission arch is open and warmly lit, showing the favorable judgment's route toward the upper realm. Across the foreground, three distinct adult Moirai performers handle one thick crimson life-thread: Clotho draws it from flax onto a spindle, Lachesis stretches the next segment along a marked measuring rod, and Atropos closes silver shears on its far end, with two freshly severed tips close beside the blades. The connected course from spindle to rod to the cutting point is fully visible; beyond the small cut gap, the same crimson strand continues to the deceased woman's medallion. A single sculptural world-axis tree fills the rear stage, its continuous trunk rising from a visible dark subterranean root chamber through an inhabited earth platform into a celestial crown under a luminous star canopy. The same tree visibly connects all three vertically separated realms. A slightly raised frontal camera keeps all six performers, both scale pans, the thread-hand contacts, root chamber, and crown in one crisp frame. Warm facial light, cool shadows, feather barbs, taut fiber, satin folds, and worn stage timber give the installation physical presence.
